thesis_at_purchase_vs_now: Entertainment spin-off catalyst: broken, management rejected the proposal [D01, D07]
Electronics turnaround: persistent disappointment, with significant goodwill impairment in mobile [D01, D03]
Sum-of-the-parts value: remains, but now requires fresh segment earnings work following the mobile forecast revision [D02, D04]
final.remaining_skew: unclear; the primary structural catalyst is gone, and earnings power is suppressed by mobile losses [D04, D07]
final.next_catalyst_and_timing: none; no structural or entertainment IPO event is on the horizon [D07]

drivers.driver: The core thesis of an entertainment spin-off was rejected by the board, rendering the primary structural catalyst spent [D07, D08].
The mobile division's substantial goodwill impairment signals lower future cash flows and prolonged electronics risk [D01, D03].
Management's shift toward a revised mobile plan offers no immediate path to re-rating, and the dividend has been eliminated [D03, D04].
We exit to rotate capital into higher-skew events now that the original governance path is closed [D04, D08].

final.memo:
The investment in Sony was underwritten on the strength of a potential entertainment spin-off and a focused electronics turnaround [D07, D08]. With the board having formally rejected the entertainment listing, the central structural catalyst for the position has been realised as a negative [D03, D07]. We do not wait for management to be proved right in the long run when the primary thesis for our involvement has been explicitly dismissed by the issuer [D07, D08].

Recent financial disclosures further degrade the investment case. The ¥180bn impairment of mobile goodwill confirms our concerns regarding the division's competitive environment and cash generation [D01, D03]. While gaming and sensors retain some value, the parent's ability to fund loss-making mobile hardware remains a drain on the consolidated entity [D04, D05]. A currency-assisted recovery is not a substitute for the structural change we originally demanded [D06].

We adhere to our discipline of exiting when the catalyst is spent or the thesis breaks [D04, D08]. Having exhausted the governance route and seeing no further actionable timetable for value unlocking, we are liquidating the position to redeploy capital into more asymmetric opportunities [D04, D08].
